prose.intro_html: Fricassee is a fancy French word for a plain good idea. You brown the chicken, build a pan sauce out of everything stuck to the bottom, then let the two finish cooking together. No special cut, no long braise, no equipment you do not already own. Boneless breasts, sliced portobello, an onion, a splash of white wine, and a little sour cream and egg yolk whisked in at the end to pull the sauce together. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is a white-tablecloth dinner priced like a weeknight.
shop_smart: Seven pounds of boneless breasts is the backbone. That is about fourteen breasts, one per serving, and it is where most of the money and all of the protein live. Reach for the big family pack instead of the small trays so you are paying for chicken, not packaging.

Three and a half pounds of portobello do the heavy flavor work. Sliced portobello browns deep and meaty, and that is what gives this sauce its body. If your store sells whole caps, buy them by weight and slice them at home.

A few onions and a head of garlic are the aromatics. You need about three and a half onions chopped fine and seven cloves of garlic. Both are cheap staples that stretch across everything else you cook.

A splash of dry white wine deglazes the pan. You only need just under a cup to lift the browned bits off the bottom. Any dry white you would actually drink works here, so skip the bottle labeled cooking wine.

Full-fat sour cream and a few egg yolks finish the sauce. Buy the real full-fat tub rather than light, because the fat is what keeps the sauce from breaking, and a carton of eggs gives you the four yolks the recipe asks for.

Butter, olive oil, flour, nutmeg, lemon, and parsley round it out. These are pantry and produce backbone you most likely already have, so they barely move the cart. Tarragon is the classic herb for fricassee if your store carries it, and parsley is the everyday stand-in when it does not.
make_it: Weigh your empty Dutch oven or deep skillet and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of eyeballing every container.
Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels and season them all over with the kosher salt and black pepper.

Melt the butter with the olive oil in the pot over medium-high heat. Working in batches so the pot is not crowded, sear the breasts about 4 minutes a side until browned. They will not be cooked through yet. Move them to a plate and cover with foil.
Add the sliced portobello, the chopped onion, and the white wine to the same pot. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the mushrooms are browned and the pan is nearly dry.
Stir in the garlic and the flour and cook one minute, scraping the browned bits up off the bottom.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring it to a boil, and let it loosen everything stuck to the pot.

Nestle the chicken and any collected juices back in, cover, and cook over medium heat until a thermometer in the thickest breast reads 160 degrees F, about 5 to 10 minutes. Move the chicken to a clean platter and cover it again.

Whisk the egg yolks and sour cream together in a small bowl. Stir a ladle of the hot pan sauce into the bowl first to warm it, then pour that mixture back into the pot, stirring the whole time so the sauce stays smooth and does not curdle.
Stir in the lemon juice, the nutmeg, and the minced parsley and let the sauce simmer 5 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt. Return the chicken to the pot and turn each piece to coat.
Weigh the full pot and subtract the empty weight from Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide by 14 and give each container one breast and an even share of the mushroom sauce, aiming for that weight.
prose.portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14. Each container gets one chicken breast and an even ladle of the mushroom sauce, landing near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.description: French chicken fricassee for meal prep: seared boneless chicken breasts finished in a creamy mushroom pan sauce with white wine, sour cream, and egg yolk, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 15 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: chicken fricassee, french chicken fricassee, low carb meal prep, high protein chicken dinner, creamy mushroom chicken
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season it with the kosher salt and black pepper.
Sear the breasts in the butter and olive oil until browned but not cooked through, then set them aside.
Cook the portobello, onion, and white wine until browned, then stir in the garlic and flour.
Add the chicken broth, bring to a boil, return the chicken, and cook to 160 degrees F.
Temper the egg yolks and sour cream with the hot pan sauce, stir the mixture back in, then add the lemon juice, nutmeg, and parsley and simmer.
Weigh the pot, subtract the empty weight, and divide across 14 containers.
